s4.champion: Primary clear-cell adenocarcinoma of the penis

raw.champion: Primary clear-cell adenocarcinoma of the penis
raw.rationale: The presence of a primary lesion on the glans penis with clear cell features and lymphovascular invasion, along with the patient's history and biopsy results, supports this diagnosis without evidence of metastasis from other known cancers.

rejected.label: Clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells with abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm is more suggestive of an adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of a primary renal cell carcinoma, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Metastatic clear-cell prostatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's prostatic adenocarcinoma was described as moderately differentiated without evidence of metastasis, and the clear cell features are not typical for prostate cancer metastasis.

rejected.label: Extramammary Paget disease
rejected.why: The presence of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells and lymphovascular invasion is not characteristic of Extramammary Paget disease, which typically involves pagetoid spread of individual cells within the epidermis.
